messages.content: Find out the rewards for playing Fortnite on Playstation platform with different missions and trophies

function.name: game_scores_get
function.description: Retrieve scores and rankings based on player’s performance in a certain game. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

platform.description: The gaming platform e.g. Xbox, Playstation, PC

level.description: The level of the game for which you want to retrieve the scores.

player.description: The name of the player for whom you want to retrieve scores. Default ''

function.name: game_rewards_get
function.description: Retrieve information about different types of rewards that you can receive when playing a certain game. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

platform.description: The gaming platform e.g. Xbox, Playstation, PC

mission.description: The mission for which you want to know the rewards. Default to ''

trophy.description: The trophy level for which you want to know the rewards. Default to ''

function.name: game_missions_list
function.description: List all missions for a certain game. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

message.reasoning:
We need to call two functions? We have get rewards for different missions and trophies. Probably we should list missions first then query each reward.

But maybe just use game_rewards_get specifying mission or trophy optional. But question says "with different missions and trophies". So likely they expect multiple calls: one per mission/trophy combination. Let's do:

1) Get list of missions via game_missions_list(game="Fortnite", platform?) Actually function signature only has game param; no platform. We'll pass game=Fortnite.

2) For each mission returned, call game_rewards_get with mission set.

Also ask for trophy levels: maybe call with trophy parameter separately.

Let's proceed stepwise. First call game_missions_list. Then parse results. Then iterate over missions calling game_rewards_get. Also call for trophy categories like Bronze, Silver etc. Use default empty if not needed.

We'll produce output after retrieving data.
